notes.title: Alex C. — Detailed Training Plan
notes.content:
Client: Alex C.
Goal: Half-marathon (sub 1:45) — Target race: San Jose Rock n Roll Half (June 14, 2026)
Training phase: Base building (March 2026)

- Monday: Strength — Lower body + core (60 min)
  - Squats: 4x8

- Tuesday: Run/Conditioning (45 min)

  - Main: Tempo intervals (4x5 min at half-marathon pace, 2 min recovery)

  - Shoulder stability work

- Saturday: Long run/conditioning (60-75 min)
  - Easy-pace long run (building from 6 to 10 miles over 8 weeks)
  - Currently at 7 miles
  - OR: hill repeats when building strength phase

Progress notes (March 2026):
- Core strength improving (plank from 45sec to 90sec)
- Hip flexor tightness persistent — added daily mobility homework
- Weight: 168 lbs (stable, healthy for his frame at 5'10")
- Resting HR: 58 bpm (good aerobic base)

Adjustments:

notes.title: Nutrition Basics — Client Handout
notes.content:
Nutrition Fundamentals — Client Reference Sheet
(Note: I provide general guidance only. For specific medical diets, refer to RD.)

Caloric needs (general guidelines):
- Fat loss: Body weight (lbs) x 10-12 calories
- Maintenance: Body weight (lbs) x 14-16 calories
- Muscle gain: Body weight (lbs) x 16-18 calories

Macronutrient guidelines:
- Protein: 0.8-1g per pound of body weight (higher end for muscle building)
- Fats: 25-35% of total calories
- Carbs: Fill remaining calories (adjust based on activity level)

Meal timing (general):
- Pre-workout (1-2 hours before): Carbs + moderate protein
- Post-workout (within 2 hours): Protein + carbs
- Before bed: Casein protein or cottage cheese (slow release)

Hydration:
- Minimum: Half body weight in ounces (150lb person = 75oz)
- Add 16-20oz per hour of exercise
- Electrolytes for sessions over 60 minutes

Supplements (evidence-based only):
- Creatine monohydrate: 5g/day (well-researched, safe)
- Protein powder: Convenience only, whole foods preferred
- Vitamin D: If deficient (common in Bay Area despite sun)
- Caffeine: 200-400mg pre-workout for performance

Common client mistakes:
- Not eating enough protein (especially women)
- Skipping meals then overeating at night
- Too many liquid calories (lattes, juice, alcohol)
- Overcomplicating it — consistency > perfection

notes.title: Meal Prep Ideas — Simple & High Protein
notes.content:
Ryan's Meal Prep Rotation

(I share these with clients who ask)

Breakfast options (prep ahead):
1. Overnight oats: Oats + protein powder + milk + berries (in jars, 5 days)
2. Egg muffins: Eggs + vegetables + cheese (baked in muffin tin, 12 at a time)
3. Protein pancakes: Blend oats + eggs + protein powder + banana (freeze in stacks)

Lunch/Dinner rotation (cook Sunday):
1. Sheet pan chicken + roasted vegetables (sweet potato, broccoli, bell peppers)
2. Turkey chili (huge batch, portion into containers)
3. Salmon + quinoa + asparagus
4. Ground beef stir-fry with rice and mixed vegetables
5. Slow cooker pulled chicken (use for wraps, bowls, salads all week)

Snacks (always have on hand):
- Greek yogurt + nuts
- Rice cakes + peanut butter
- Protein bars (RXBar or Barebells)
- Hard-boiled eggs
- String cheese + apple

Grocery budget: ~$150/week (high protein food is expensive)

Philosophy: Simple, repeatable, sufficient protein. I don't need gourmet — I need consistent fuel. Save the restaurant meals for weekends and social occasions.

Shared with Alex C. after he asked for nutrition help. He said he barely has time to eat — I told him meal prep takes 2 hours on Sunday and saves 10+ decisions per week.
